outcome.answer:
A direct “GNN proxy for SDP relaxations” is addressed in the Max-Cut setting: Chen, Qian, Morris, et al. propose a Max-Cut-specific graph neural network that acts as a lightweight, validity-preserving neural proxy for the semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations used inside exact branch-and-bound. The model predicts both primal- and dual-feasible SDP solutions and yields feasible Max-Cut solutions via the Goemans–Williamson algorithm, allowing it to be plugged into an exact solver framework. It is trained self-supervised (without requiring solved SDP relaxations as labels) and empirically reduces the cost of bounding by up to 10.6× versus using Mosek. [2]

Qian and Morris study when GNNs can (or cannot) recover SDP solutions, proving negative results for standard GNN architectures on linear SDPs and identifying a more expressive architecture that can emulate updates of a standard first-order solver; it also reports speedups when using learned predictions to warm-start a first-order solver. This is more about expressivity and optimization recovery than a Max-Cut-style drop-in SDP solver proxy. [1]
